answer: A market for nebula images, jade sales and gale alerts admits keys through a bandwidth test. Independent testers send a different random stream per key. After cutoff, random byte queries with a tight deadline check receipt; missing bytes fail admission. Each extra key must receive B fresh bytes within T seconds. Unpredictable streams prevent replay and multicast reuse: parallel aliases still need aggregate bandwidth nB/T. Sampling k positions catches a client retaining only fraction f with probability 1-f^k. Honest testers are essential; wholesale bandwidth remains an advantage.
